body:
Before: Draft #90 cut test release 1.1.0-rc.5 with one change, the clock-change choice (#87, ZOD-66). An independent review of #90 found a fault in the package: when a caller asked for the later pass of a time that was not repeated (an ordinary time, or a time the clocks skipped), the result was right but the receipt still said "later". Earlier engines (1.1.0-rc.1 and 1.1.0-rc.3 were run) refuse any receipt that says "later", so those receipts were unreadable by them for no reason, and the CHANGELOG's sentence that the option "changes nothing for a time the clock showed once" was not true. A packed archive can never be edited or repacked, so rc.5 cannot be corrected in place.

After: This is test release 1.1.0-rc.6 as a draft. It replaces #89 and #90. It carries the clock-change choice with that fault fixed:
- A birth in an hour the clock showed twice (clocks going back) can take the later pass, with `fold: "later"` in `@zodiacs/engine/geo`. The default is unchanged. Example: 01:30 in New York on 2021-11-07 resolves to 06:30 UTC with `fold: "later"` and to 05:30 UTC without it.
- The fix: the receipt now says "later" only when the time really was repeated and the later pass was asked for. Asking for the later pass of any other time gives exactly the result and the receipt you get without asking, and earlier engines read it.

It does not contain #88. In 1.x a birth given as a bare date such as `"1990-05-03"` is still read as midnight UTC, as documented. The refusal is held for 2.0.0 by your decision of 11 November 2026.

Nothing is published. No npm publish, no tag, no GitHub release, and the release workflow was not run.

What changed since rc.5, and why:
1. The fix above (`src/geo/timezone.ts`, commit `444666f`). The reviewer's main finding.
2. The receipt reader now also refuses a receipt that says "later" for a time that was not repeated, as `invalid_context` (`src/receipt.ts`). This engine never writes such a receipt, so this is a consistency check only: a "later" record now always means a real second pass.
3. `docs/versioning.md` now says plainly that the allowed values of this one receipt field were widened without a new conventions set, and that earlier engines refuse the new value and do not misread it.
4. More tests (not in the package): receipts of the later pass written and read back for Lord Howe (a half-hour change), Sydney, São Paulo and New York in 1883 with and without a birthplace; an old-format receipt that says "later" is refused; an ordinary and a skipped time asked for "later" give the same receipt as unasked; the altered-receipt cases check the exact error code. The suite is 4,203 tests passed, 3 skipped (rc.5: 4,193).
5. The records (`docs/evidence/1.1.0-rc.6-20261111/`, `artifacts/README.md`, CHANGELOG) name the workflow runs and say which review has happened and which has not.

Numbering: rc.4 was drafted in #89 with the bare-date refusal and not merged. rc.5 was drafted in #90 and is superseded by this before merging. Neither archive is on this branch, and both numbers are skipped, because an archive is never repacked under a number it has already had.

How: A new branch from main (`bc0b5a7`, which has not moved). #87's branch is merged in with a merge commit (its commit `3ea3e98` is kept). Then the fix and its tests (`444666f`). Then the source commit (`c3efe91`): version 1.1.0-rc.6 everywhere, the CHANGELOG entry, the README lines, the two size limits, regenerated conformance results (only the version string changes) and the evidence. This time the checks ran on GitHub on the source commit before the archive was packed into the branch, and all 28 passed (CI run 43014592658, Conformance 43014592715, Atlas 43014592797). Then the commit that carries the archive (`7210037`), then one that records the checks (`ce4ba82`).

The archive: `artifacts/zodiacs-engine-1.1.0-rc.6.tgz`, SHA-256 `648714ca7485c7381f338286b84a211752ddd425035f50f6e24267e80de6abde`, 333,982 bytes, 94 files (1,148,327 bytes unpacked), packed from source commit `c3efe9175644ee6a0d9f40e2d9fa0766aa264fa6`. Clean clones of that commit packed the same bytes on Node 22.22.2, 20.19.0 and 24.21.0.

Size limits: the two you approved on 11 November 2026, unchanged. Nothing more is asked for.
- `./geo`: limit 35,600 bytes. It measures 35,584 (rc.5: 35,574). The fix alone would have made it 35,610, over the limit, so the same commit writes one neighbouring line in a shorter form (the flag name is built from the kind of jump, which gives the same two flags and changes no value). Headroom is 0.04 per cent, so the next change to this entry will need a new limit.
- Whole package: limit 1,150,000 bytes. It measures 1,148,327 (rc.5: 1,147,669; the extra is mostly the longer CHANGELOG entry). Headroom 0.14 per cent.

Tests: Run locally on the commit that carries the archive: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `exports:smoke`, `api:check`, `package:contents`, `pack:dry-run` on Node 22.22.2; `node scripts/verify-archive-binding.mjs` on Node 20.19.0, 22.22.2 and 24.21.0 (each rebuilt the archive byte for byte); `--rebuild-all` on Node 22.22.2 (all 19 recorded archives rebuild from their source commits); the packed-consumer check on the carried archive on Node 20.19.0, 22.22.2 and 24.21.0; the conformance and atlas checks on Node 22.22.2. Evidence: `later-receipt-on-rc3.json` and `later-receipt-on-rc1.json` show that 1.1.0-rc.3 and 1.1.0-rc.1 refuse only the receipt of a real later pass, and read the receipt of an ordinary time and of a skipped time asked for "later". Engines before 1.1.0-rc.1 were not run.

Owner decisions:
1. Merging. If you accept this candidate, merge it with a merge commit, never squash or rebase: `archives.json` records the source commit, and a squash would break the archive check for good. The archive is immutable from now on. If anything in the package needs to change, that is 1.1.0-rc.7, not an edit here.
2. This replaces #89 and #90 and supersedes #87. #89 and #90 should be closed without merging (merging either would carry a second candidate). #87 can be closed after this merges. #88 stays open as the draft for 2.0.0, or can be closed and redone then. I closed none of them.
3. Reviews. The independent review of rc.5 is done and acted on here. The fix in this candidate changes what a receipt records, so it needs its own independent review, which has not happened yet. If that review finds anything in the package, the fix is 1.1.0-rc.7.
4. The stricter receipt check (item 2 above) is a choice. A receipt that the rc.5 draft would have written for an ordinary time asked for "later" is now refused. rc.5 was never merged or published, so no such receipt should exist. Say so if you would rather the reader stayed lenient.
5. A date passed on its own, and a birth given as a bare date, are both read as midnight UTC in 1.x. Whether `saturnReturn` and the progressions should also refuse a bare date is part of the 2.0.0 question, with #88.
6. From #87, still open: a "later" receipt is accepted whatever engine version it names; `lunarReturn` still refuses a birth flagged `dst-fold` even when a pass was chosen. (The third item of that list, the receipt recording the pass asked for when the time was not repeated, is what this candidate fixes.)
7. Site follow-up, not done here (no site change): the site vendors 1.1.0-rc.2. To offer the choice of pass it would need to vendor this candidate, pass `fold` through `src/lib/time/localToUtc.ts`, and ask "which one?" in the birth form. Letting the connector's natal chart tool choose the pass means changing a published tool definition, which is your call.

Linear: ZOD-66
